💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 09:10 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • But if you search for it, there is footage.
  • According to recent reports, of all the games played by Jason Wilcox and Mauricio Pochettino, this was the sole example of them sharing a pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 09:10 EST, 14 November 2026.

It only happened once. But if you search for it, there is footage. The date was February 23, 2000 and the place was the old Wembley Stadium. England 0-0 Argentina, the kind of friendly best forgotten, except for a single line of trivia.

According to recent reports, of all the games played by Jason Wilcox and Mauricio Pochettino, this was the sole example of them sharing a pitch. Wilcox was given the full 90 at a point when Kevin Keegan was low on options for the left wing and Pochettino came on with 35 minutes on the clock and kicked a few people.

He was good at kicking people, Pochettino. He flattened Paul Scholes once, then he nudged over David Beckham and twice he got stuck into Emile Heskey. But Wilcox was in a safe zone on the other side of the field that night. While Pochettino indulged his hobby, Wilcox kept out of harm’s way.

We might ask at this juncture if either of them ever changed their spots. But it’s more interesting to ponder what comes next, now they have been pitched together again at Manchester United.

According to recent reports, united needed a big bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one. Wilcox’s preference? Well, United’s director of hopeless football quite fancied Eddie Howe, according to the whispers, and Howe is far from a shrinking violet, but he’s not Pochettino. And Pochettino certainly isn’t Carrick.

According to recent reports, pochettino won’t drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run. And he won’t have the same patience for incompetence from those below or above.

Manchester United needed a massive bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one in Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino is not the sort of manager to drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run, like Carrick did this week.

With any luck, United knew this when they reached an agreement that was a decade in the making. If they did, it would demonstrate some self-awareness at last, because United have badly needed the right blend of bruiser and diplomat in that seat.

They have cried out for someone who isn’t too nice, too loyal, too whiny or too undermined by their own shortcomings to have the kind of rucks that are needed for change. By that logic, United may have invited their own worst enemy to dinner, or their best chance of a solution.

Sources indicate that there have been few managerial appointments in recent years as inherently fascinating as this one. That instinct is partly driven by the thought it has all arrived a touch late – when United favoured Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to replace Jose Mourinho, it was a sliding-door moment for all parties.

Recent findings suggest that but there’s another way of viewing this and that comes from the opposite angle. Maybe this is the perfect time, based on the qualifications needed to operate within the modern version of United.

There is no doubt that Pochettino has lost some of his sheen since his masterful handling of Daniel Levy at Tottenham, but what did he gain? He managed the vastest collection of footballing egos at PSG, worked under a convoluted tier of meddlers in the madhouse of Chelsea and was confronted by presidential interference in his time with the US national team at the World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that two schools of thought can exist here. One is that he failed to tear up any trees in each of those assignments. But the other talks to the point we are making: United require a manager who can navigate their unique brand of chaos and the upcoming guy knows the dance.

Pochettino won’t ever thank Donald Trump for the Folarin Balogun fiasco in the summer, but Sir Jim Ratcliffe would have to work awfully hard to cause him a more uncomfortable press conference.

The scale of Pochettino’s challenge is obvious. In the micro, that means applying a playing style built on hard running to a squad that jogged its way to embarrassing statistics under Carrick. In the macro, it will be his challenge with Wilcox and a recruitment team that effectively cost Carrick his job.

Pochettino has had plenty to deal with as USA coach, not least the meddling of Donald Trump.

Pochettino has the authority to challenge (above, from left) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox over United's failing transfer policy.

Talking to one of Pochettino’s former colleagues on Friday, the expectation is that greater control over transfers will have been a key tenet of those negotiations with United.

As predictable as that might sound, it was a huge bone of contention for him at Chelsea and United’s failures in this area are clear. Time will tell if any promises are honoured.

In a recent development, but Pochettino has got what he wanted and pursued. His desire for the post has never been disguised, which can be mapped as a trail of breadcrumbs from that bottle of red he once shared with Sir Alex Ferguson all the way up to carefully planted mentions of the club in gatherings with media.

There were some acts of reassurance necessary for the final step, of course, and doubtless it will sting to leave the US - his farewell tears on Friday demonstrated as much. But not enough to inspire a second thought.

To look back over Pochettino’s other stints in England, one main memory stands out from his time at Tottenham and I’ve cited it in this space previously.

It has been revealed that it traces to September 2016, when Pochettino was on the rise and had a game approaching against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City. In attempting to coax a decent line in the press conference, a few of us killed time before his arrival by digging up old footage of Pochettino’s Espanyol beating Barcelona, when he and Guardiola were on opposing sides.

Recent findings suggest that within the clip was an unexpected gem, because Pochettino murdered the Brazilian Ronaldo in a challenge. He took the ball, sure, but demolished the man, too, and his boot ended up shoulder-high. We were watching this when Pochettino wandered over and requested a replay – when it was shown, he laughed maniacally.

As a player, he always saw the value in a good reducer. And it’s a trait that might well be needed at United. If Wilcox and the other cronies upstairs don’t up their game, they might find that Carrington offers fewer hiding places than the old Wembley.

Pochettino's fondness for the USA job was apparent by his farewell tears on Friday.

Was Tom Brady ever in the Blues' building?

Industry observers note that tom Brady has left Birmingham, but was he ever really there? Across three years, he attended only four games.

The club is on a steep upward trajectory and there is no doubt that the Brady association helped on their commercial side.

In a recent development, but I recall speaking to one Blues shareholder a couple of seasons back, and after attempting to establish some tangible detail about their star investor’s contribution, there was a period of silence. When I asked how often Brady might dial into meetings, there was laughter.

In this era of celebrity ownership of our football clubs, it’s easy to get blinded by a famous name. And easier still to get drawn in by suggestions of expertise that they have carried over from a different space.

But in the vast majority of cases, they are little more than mascots without the costume.

Tom Brady makes a rare appearance at a Birmingham match in 2025.

Great delivery from Cummins - but it's not over yet.

Pat Cummins stood for 70 minutes on Thursday and answered questions about Sandpapergate.

The Australia captain refused to budge, both from the microphone and his position that Usman Khawaja was incorrect in his claim that the entire team was in on the plot to cheat against South Africa in 2018.

It’s hard to know what was more impressive – Cummins’ commitment to answering every question, or his delusion in believing that it would be the last time he discusses it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton made it five games unbeaten with a hard-fought goalless draw away at high-flying Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday afternoon.

The result sees the Blues continue their strong form having thrashed Durham 6-0 on Wednesday following two stalemates against Chelsea and Manchester United in the WSL.

Ruby Mace grabbed the Player of the Match award in the capital – the midfielder repeating her award-winning performance at the home of the North Londoners last term.

Recent findings suggest that it was the visitors who created the first real opportunity inside 17 minutes as Ornella Vignola teed the in-form Yuka Momiki on the edge of the area. The forward, who netted a hat-trick in the 6-0 win in midweek, looked to curl past Lize Kop, but saw her placed effort saved by the diving keeper.

According to recent reports, history repeated itself only ten minutes later as Momiki saw another strike palmed away by the keeper. The 30-year-old drifted inside from the right and let fly upon reaching the edge of the box. Unfortunately, Kop anticipated the shot and collected after initially spilling the ball.

In a recent development, the hosts responded on 39 minutes as Courtney Brosnan was called in to action to deny Julie Blakstad. After breaching the Blues’ box, the Norwegian feinted before unleashing a rising strike at goal. Brosnan leapt up to tip the ball over the upright, though.

That concluded the action for a tight, physical opening 45; with Blakstad coming close once more five minutes after the interval.

Recent findings suggest that found at the back-post, the winger fired at goal and seemed destined to get on the scoresheet. However, Hannah Blundell burst forward to narrow the angle and bravely block, evading the danger.

At the other end, Everton caught Spurs on the break after Momiki held the ball up well on the halfway line. Clare Wheeler threaded it through to the advancing Vignola, who raced at goal with the ball at her feet. She pulled the trigger when faced one-on-one with Kop, but saw her low-strike sail agonisingly wide of the far-post.

Industry observers note that brosnan produced another fine stop five minutes later, the keeper denying Cathinka Tandenberg on this occasion. The Norway-international got down low in an attempt to nestle the ball in to the bottom right corner. Somehow, Brosnan reacted rapidly to palm it away for a corner.

According to recent reports, moments later, Blakstad threatened again – the forward rattling the upright on this occasion. She cut-in past Rosa van Gool and let fly, the ball striking the frame of the goal on its way out.

Head coach Scott Phelan made his first change of the game with 12 minutes remaining as Noemie Mouchon, who scored a brace against Durham on Wednesday, replaced Momiki.

Recent findings suggest that the striker almost had an instant impact as she forced Kop in to a smart save. Rion Ishikawa did brilliantly down the unfamiliar right to dance past two challenges before chipping it through to the substitute. Mouchon came inside before unleashing a curling effort that was caught well by the retreating Kop.

According to recent reports, the France-youth international came even closer in the dying minutes as she had a chance similar to Vignola previously. Like her teammate, Mouchon’s strike whistled just wide of the far-post from the right-hand side of the box.

The referee then concluded the affair, with attention now turning to Everton’s Players Cup tie with Manchester United on Wednesday night (7pm KO).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • FIGC Special Commissioner Giovanni Malagò warns Italy is made of ’60 million coaches’ who all have their opinions, but hits back at those who want ‘old-school Italian defending and counter-attacks.’.
  • The Azzurri came back to earth with a thud last night, as after beating France 3-1 at San Siro to go top of the Nations League group, they were thumped 4-1 by Belgium and failed to reach the quarter-finals.
  • “We always tend to see things in the most negative way, and while this is certainly a wake-up call, I always said we needed to keep our feet on the ground,” Malagò told reporters including Football Italia when attending the Panchina D’Oro awards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FIGC Special Commissioner Giovanni Malagò warns Italy is made of ’60 million coaches’ who all have their opinions, but hits back at those who want ‘old-school Italian defending and counter-attacks.’.

The Azzurri came back to earth with a thud last night, as after beating France 3-1 at San Siro to go top of the Nations League group, they were thumped 4-1 by Belgium and failed to reach the quarter-finals.

“We always tend to see things in the most negative way, and while this is certainly a wake-up call, I always said we needed to keep our feet on the ground,” Malagò told reporters including Football Italia when attending the Panchina D’Oro awards.

“It’s not as if Italy turned into a phenomenal team in the space of five or six months, so it is part of the process. These are defeats we’d rather avoid, obviously, but they are undoubtedly a teachable moment too.”.

When Malagò appointed coach Roberto Mancini for his second spell, there was a great deal of doubt around the decision, but the 3-1 victory over France showed immense progress.

“There is an incredible number of Italians watching us, and everyone is now discovering young talents who are pushing their way onto the international stage. You don’t need to know much about football to realise these will be protagonists of the future, but it will take time.”.

Some of Mancini’s tactics have also been criticised after the 4-1 defeat to Belgium, a game where a draw would’ve been enough to qualify for the Nations League knockout phase.

“What we did confirm is that Italy has 60 million coaches, everyone has their own view on how things ought to be done,” added Malagò.

“Many maintain that we should go back to old-school Italian defending and counter-attacks, which was certainly the school of thought that made history of football, and occasionally some foreign coaches make fun of us for that.

“The truth is, that style is passe. Modern football is technical, tactical, but also physical. It’s no coincidence we’re seeing so many injuries now with three games per week. The tempo of the game has increased by a lot, and perhaps that is where we need to find the right balance.

“We mustn’t be too attached to the tactical systems of the past that don’t get us far, but at the same time when the opponents are stronger on paper, we’ve got to think of something on a tactical level to even it out. When it comes to that aspect, we need lessons from nobody.”.

Malagò is currently the Special Commissioner of the FIGC awaiting the latest election on December 14, but will be up against former Milan and Monza CEO Adriano Galliani.

There was the possibility that Galliani would try to rule the latest Malagò candidacy illegitimate too over confusion around the status of Genoa’s backing, but decided to withdraw the appeal.

“It was an important sign to calm the waters, and it is what I expected,” said the former FIGC President whose first June election was ruled irregular due to the lack of paperwork for his original candidacy.

“Hopefully now we can only talk about the election with a sense of calm and gentlemanly behaviour.”.

While many national associations have urged Infantino to step down, and Italy have also withdrawn their support for him, they have so far struggled to find anyone willing to run against him in the next election who could gain significant backing.

Infantino has so far been able to weather numerous controversies and storms, above all the attempt to privatise some of the World Cup tournaments, and that is largely thanks to the support he has from those nations outside Europe.

It remains to be seen if Diallo will encourage enough nations to switch their vote away from Infantino.

The Premier League is set to introduce a upcoming LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

Stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, rolled out in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences.".

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent matter.

Controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â.

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped aims for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players presently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs fresh campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

Breaking: The four problems Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix at Man United: From substantial names causing unrest in the dressing room to an problem which plagued Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick before him, these are the items top of his Old Trafford in-tray

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.
  • The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.

With United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League standings, it’s clear why Pochettino has been brought in to replace Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the most pressing matters in Pochettino’s in-tray at Carrington as the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss and his backroom staff head for Manchester...

Mauricio Pochettino is the new manager of Manchester United - but the problems he has to fix are already piling up.

It sounds obvious, but winning games to get United out of the Premier League drop zone has to be the first priority.

Everything at a football club flows from the results on the pitch, and United’s humiliating decline this season has had ramifications throughout Old Trafford and Carrington.

The players are clearly low on confidence which has only exacerbated the team’s dismal performances and brought just one win in 10 Premier League games, against newly-promoted Ipswich – United’s worst start in 40 years.

Diogo Dalot is a prime example, after fans cheered his substitution in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, and the defender cut a crestfallen figure as he left Old Trafford to go on international duty with Portugal.

The Stretford End also turned on the players as the atmosphere turned toxic after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth at the end of last month, having vented their anger towards the club’s ownership – the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at every opportunity.

That won’t go away anytime soon, but a winning team will at least take some of the sting out of the situation if appointing Pochettino can give United a ‘bounce’ and divert attention back onto the pitch.

United players are low on confidence, not least Diogo Dalot (left) whose substitution was cheered by his own fans against Aston Villa.

The United team were also lambasted by the Stretford End after the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last month.

Carrick enjoyed a good start, losing just two of his 17 games in charge in the second half of last season to earn a two-year contract, but United struggled under him this term due to a combination of poor recruitment, injuries and lack of fitness.

According to recent reports, these are all problems that Pochettino must try to put right. There is little he can do about recruitment until the January transfer window opens and United have a chance to atone for their mistake in not signing cover at left back and centre forward last summer, which backfired spectacularly when both Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko picked up injuries.

He can, however, try to get more out of United’s £155million midfield signings Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again – Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and a United squad that was good enough to finish third in the Premier League last season.

Injuries have been a major problem with the hamstring strain that will keep Baleba out of action for Pochettino’s first few weeks in charge just the latest setback.

As well as Shaw, Sesko, Baleba and long-term casualty Manuel Ugarte, United have also lost Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui for parts of this season.

Pochettino must get more out of United’s £155million midfield signing Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again.

United have struggled to keep up with their opponents since the opening day - a lack of fitness has plagued every manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Industry observers note that the good news for Pochettino is that Shaw and Rashford are hoping to be fit for Anfield, while Matthijs de Ligt is available again after a year out with back problems. However, Sesko’s absence until the upcoming year leaves the new boss without his most natural source of goals.

Fitness is another matter and United have looked short of it since the opening-day defeat at Hull City amid concerns that the coaching levels dropped off under Carrick and were too relaxed.

They covered 120.8 kilometres against Villa – the most in a league game under Carrick – and Pochettino will demand that and a whole lot more as he increases the work-rate among his new squad.

It’s a problem that has hindered a succession of United bosses going back to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and the Argentine must find a way to drill a better work ethic into United.

The problems at United this season have inevitably led to unrest in the dressing room, with the biggest issue centred around captain Bruno Fernandes.

News that Fernandes has rejected United’s latest contract offer has come as no surprise given his dramatic change in fortunes from last season, and Pochettino must find a way to get arguably United’s best player back in form and onside.

Having set a upcoming Premier League record for assists and picked up a string of player of the year awards last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off a cliff as he struggled with an injury sustained at the World Cup, and he suffered the rare indignity of being benched for the loss to Bournemouth.

Never one to hide his mood very well, the 32-year-old criticised Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat by Como in what was a major blow to his head coach.

Never one to hide his mood very well, Bruno Fernandes has been disgruntled of late and rejected United's offer of a new contract.

Lisandro Martinez looks to be headed for the exit door - although the arrival of his fellow Argentine Pochettino may help things.

While the United hierarchy will try to persuade Fernandes to sign a new deal in keeping with their reduced wage structure and the fact he will turn 33 next year, Pochettino has to find a way of relighting the fire in his skipper.

According to recent reports, whether the club will make as much effort to keep Lisandro Martinez as he comes towards the end of his contract remains to be seen after another member of United’s leadership team took aim at Wilcox’s recruitment after the defeat by Atletico Madrid. It is mentioned to have caused an angry clash between Martinez and summer signing Tielemans on the way back from Spain.

Martinez looks to be heading for the Old Trafford exit, but it will be interesting to see if the arrival of his compatriot Pochettino – a combative Argentine centre back in much the same mould as a player – has an impact on that.

As a former defender, Pochettino won’t need telling that leaking 15 goals in the last five games simply isn’t good enough. United have now let in 30 in all competitions this season, the most of any club in Europe’s top five leagues apart from Lens.

Recent findings suggest that they have been appalling at the back, conceding in the opening seconds to Atletico, Como and Villa. Had they been able to hold out and prevent late equalisers against Everton and Tottenham, the additional four points would have them 12th in the table rather than in the relegation zone.

A revolving door of makeshift left backs in the absence of Shaw and Dorgu, De Ligt’s belated comeback and Martinez’s needless red card at Chelsea haven’t helped.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens, so composed last season, looks considerably more shaky behind a leaky and ever-changing back-four, and had arguably his worst game against Villa last weekend.

Pochettino couldn’t ask for a tougher first test than going to Anfield, and knows that United will have to start by being solid at the back.

The 22-year-old has established himself as an vital player for Stuttgart since joining the German club, impressing with his technical ability, creativity and versatility in attacking positions.

El Khannouss registered 16 goal contributions in 41 appearances last season, helping Stuttgart secure Champions League qualification. He has continued his impressive performances this campaign, scoring twice in his first nine appearances.

Farke is reportedly a huge admirer of the midfielder, having monitored his development at Leicester City. His ability to operate as a No.10 or on either wing could add another dimension to Leeds’ final third.

The Whites have made a decent start to the Premier League campaign, but adding more creativity and attacking quality could help them maintain their momentum.

However, convincing Stuttgart to part ways with their highly rated midfielder will not be straightforward.

Industry observers note that TEAMtalk claims the Bundesliga club has told Leeds they have no intention of selling El Khannouss during the January transfer window. Stuttgart consider him an important part of their aims as they pursue another successful domestic campaign and progress in the Champions League.

The German side value the Moroccan at around €40 million (£33.4m), a figure that Leeds could potentially afford.

Meanwhile, the player’s representatives are open to discussions, although El Khannouss would want assurances over regular playing time before considering a move.

A summer transfer could therefore be a more realistic possibility for Leeds. If Farke remains determined to reunite with the talented midfielder, the Yorkshire outfit may have to wait until the end of the season to secure his signature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan are breathing a sigh of relief after reports Mike Maignan underwent tests in France showing there is no serious injury, so he could play against Frosinone on Sunday.

The goalkeeper started for France last night in the 2-0 Nations League victory over Turkiye, but went off at half-time.

It had been suggested there was a muscular injury with adductor pain, so it would require tests to understand the extent of the damage.

According to L’Equipe, initial tests today have been reassuring, highlighting only discomfort and no lesion or even a strain.

It is believed that coming off at half-time prevented the situation getting any worse, so Maignan could be available for this Sunday’s Serie A match against Frosinone.

The Rossoneri were particularly concerned because their second choice goalkeeper Pietro Terracciano has been out injured for several weeks already.

It means if the captain had not recovered in time, then Lorenzo Torriani would’ve been given his Serie A debut this weekend.

Torriani already stepped in for the Europa League after Maignan was sent off in the game with Bournemouth and then suspended for the defeat to Ferencvaros.

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

In a recent development, roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

It has been revealed that and then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

In a recent development, united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

It has been revealed that whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Recent findings suggest that carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

He had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

It has been revealed that from being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

Industry observers note that the difference to those opening 45 minutes was as stark as it gets. Indeed, the first half felt like a continuation from the fans of their blood-letting against Bournemouth.

When the clock hit 20.05 – a nod to the year 2005 when the Glazers bought the club – a pile of tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch from the Stretford End amid chants of “We Want Glazers Out”. They were quickly followed by cries of “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” and “sell the club and f--- off home”.

Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, again copped for it. A banner read: “For the love, not the ‘likes’”. When the Champions League music played, hundreds of green and gold balloons – a reference to the club’s original colours and the 2010 protest movement – were released.

On the pitch, United were all over the place. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

At that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

According to recent reports, “It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” mentioned Carrick.

“I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

In a recent development, asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

Industry observers note that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys demonstrated an awful lot,” he said.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he revealed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

According to recent reports, “It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

“But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

Industry observers note that “It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, big character, big fight.”.

“We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

In a recent development, as for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we highlighted what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

Manchester United fans are planning a series of in-stadium demonstrations at Old Trafford tonight in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s ownership.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been plans to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No upcoming stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

A separate fans’ group has also been encouraging fans to join in anti Glazers and Ratcliffe chants in the 21st minute or, more specifically, after 20 minutes and 5 seconds: 20.05 is a nod to 2005, the year the Glazers completed their hostile takeover at Old Trafford.

Your United team for tonight's #UCL clash 👊 https://t.co/TD9F6RjeAB.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The United manager has opted to pair Ayden Heaven in central defence with Harry Maguire for the Roma game with Martinez dropping to the bench.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Speaking with her, former United legend Wayne Rooney has stated the Argentine has “simply not been good enough” and should not necessarily feature again under Carrick.

When Alan Shearer was asked if he would include Martínez on a team sheet tonight, he did not mince his words, calling him a “liability”.

Ahead of the confirmed line-ups coming out shortly, there are certain players we know we will not be seeing today.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no new concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

It’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Lisandro Martinez is shown a second yellow card following a VAR review 🟥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max ➡️https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/VLcAMNdqgZ.

All in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. If the beleaguered manager has any hope at all of hanging on to his job, he needs convincing results tonight and against Aston Villa on the weekend.

Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

The visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They got off to a slow start in Europe, drawing with Fernebahce in their opening match but coming agonisingly close to stunning Real Madrid on matchday two at home. They went 3-1 up before three late goals snatched victory for Madrid.

They bounced back with a convincing 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava and their domestic campaign is off to an incredibly promising start. They are right now unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

In a recent development, it has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Feel free to drop us your score predictions in the comments – bragging rights on the line for the winner.

We’ll be bringing you team news, previews from the managers and more ahead of kick-off at 8pm!

Latest Update: Even giant anteaters in remote Brazil have microplastics in their blood

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Giant anteaters traipsing across Brazil’s pristine wetlands and savannahs have ingested traces of plastic pollutants.
  • Some of Brazil’s wildlife have traces of plastic circulating in their blood — even if they live far from land used by humans, according to an analysis published on 11 November in Nature1.
  • According to recent reports, researchers measured the concentration of microplastics in the blood of 47 animals: 26 lowland tapirs (Tapirus terrestris) and 21 giant anteaters (Myrmecophaga tridactyla).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Giant anteaters traipsing across Brazil’s pristine wetlands and savannahs have ingested traces of plastic pollutants. Credit: Sylvain Cordier/Gamma-Rapho via Getty.

Some of Brazil’s wildlife have traces of plastic circulating in their blood — even if they live far from land used by humans, according to an analysis published on 11 November in Nature1.

According to recent reports, researchers measured the concentration of microplastics in the blood of 47 animals: 26 lowland tapirs (Tapirus terrestris) and 21 giant anteaters (Myrmecophaga tridactyla). The scientists found that, on average, the creatures carry similar levels of plastic as many humans — roughly 74 particles per millilitre of blood. The animals that lived closest to human infrastructure and waste-management facilities had the highest levels of microplastics in their blood.

According to recent reports, but even those living more than 100 kilometres from a waste sites and 65 kilometres from human infrastructure revealed traces of the pollutants. This indicates that plastics can reach wildlife living far from where the pollution originates, indicates study co-author Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, a conservation scientist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus in Kelowna, Canada.

The findings are an crucial step to better understand how the particles impact wildlife, says Sofia Ya-Hsuan Liou, a geochemist at the National Taiwan University in Taipei.

According to recent reports, microplastics are tiny particles (smaller than five millimetres across) with many different chemical compositions. They can travel through the environment in rainwater, rivers and the atmosphere. Although several studies have measured microplastics levels in wildlife, few have explored how the surrounding environment influences what animals ingest, says study co-author Michael Noonan, a quantitative ecologist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus.

In a recent development, to find out, Noonan, Ferraz and their colleagues collected and analysed blood samples from animals living across the Amazon rainforest, the Cerrado savannah and the huge and pristine Pantanal wetland between February 2021 and November 2022. The researchers also used GPS data to track the animals’ movements and their exposure to a human footprint.

Chelsea are reportedly still interested in signing Juventus attacking midfielder Kerim Alajbegovic despite missing out on the highly-rated youngster during the summer transfer window.

According to a TEAMtalk report, the Blues continue to monitor the 19-year-old Bosnian international, with the club considering another approach ahead of next summer.

Chelsea were among the leading contenders to secure his services earlier this year, but Alajbegovic ultimately chose Juventus in a deal worth up to €40 million. The former Bayer Leverkusen prospect has since made an encouraging start in Italy, scoring twice for the Turin outfit.

According to recent reports, the teenager previously impressed during his spell with Red Bull Salzburg, registering 13 goals in 44 appearances last season. His performances, alongside his displays at the World Cup, have further enhanced his reputation as one of Europe’s most promising young attacking talents.

It has been revealed that chelsea are looking to strengthen their attacking options, and Alajbegovic could prove to be an excellent long-term investment. His versatility and ability to operate in different attacking positions would give the London club another useful option.

Unlike the previous proposal, which involved potentially sending him to sister club Strasbourg, Chelsea are now considering a pathway that would bring the youngster into their first-team aims.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's the end of an era: Cristiano Ronaldo, the Portuguese soccer star, announced his decision to retire from the Portuguese national team. Ronaldo, who will turn 42 next year, is considered one of the best players in the history of the sport, and announced his retirement from international soccer after 23 years representing Portugal, winning Euro 2016 and two editions of the UEFA Nations League. Cristiano followed the decision of his long-time rival Lionel Messi, who retired from the Argentine national team last month. Over his career with Portugal, he scored 146 goals in 234 games.

Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh.

Ronaldo's decision follows a rift with the current head coach Jorge Jesus. Last month, the striker left Portugal's training camp aboard his private jet following a disagreement with the coach, followed by an open letter and apologies to the fans and the team where he explained his decision, without mentioning the manager. The Portuguese federation later suspended the player for 30 days but he was eligible to be called for the upcoming games against Denmark and Wales.

Ronaldo posted a video message on his social media announcing his decision to retire from the national team: "To the Portuguese people, the day has come to hand back the number seven shirt of the national team that belongs to us all. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and taking it with me to stadiums all over the world. Today the time has come to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made solely with the head; they are also made with the heart.".

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner played his sixth and last World Cup this summer in the United States, Canada and Mexico, when Portugal were eliminated by Spain in the round of 16 of the tournament.

Sources indicate that "A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever is coming to an end. When I look back and think of everything I've experienced with the national team, I don't just see matches, goals, records or trophies. I see people. I see immigrants who, for 90 minutes, felt Portugal was a little bit closer. I see millions of Portuguese people whom I've never met in person, but who have been part of my life. Because, at the end of the day, football is so much more than just a game. Football is about the people. Throughout my entire career with the national team, I've strived to push my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history," he mentioned.

"I've always been hard on myself. I've always wanted more; I've always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt. There were perfect afternoons and evenings; there were victories I'll never forget. There were defeats that I still find hard to recall today. I also failed, I also suffered, and there were moments when I wasn't able to give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal. Over the years, I've learnt some very simple things. Goals come and go, trophies end up in museums, and records are eventually broken. But there is one thing that time can never erase: the place we hold in people's hearts. If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget your worries, and feel nothing but pride in our country, then it was all worth it. Because that's what being Portuguese is all about. We suffer together, we rise together. No captain walks alone and you're all part of my story. Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, newly introduced generations who believe it's possible to reach places no one has reached before. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the United States men's national team to win their first Concacaf Gold Cup since 2021, they'll now need to contend with a latest format in the 2027 edition. The tournament will run from June 17 through July 11, with major changes coming to the group stage. It will still include only 16 teams, but instead of those teams being split into four groups of four teams each, they'll now be split into only two eight-team groups. Fifteen of those teams will qualify via the Gold Cup preliminary round and join guest nation Saudi Arabia in the tournament.

That shift has the goal of making the group stage more exciting, as not only does it add an extra game due to each team playing four teams instead of three, but it also allows a chance for chaos, as four teams will go through to the knockouts from each group. While the new game is added, that won't change how the knockouts look, as those will proceed as normal.

Sources indicate that "The Gold Cup is our region's premier men's national team competition, and we are really excited about what this upcoming format will bring to the tournament's Group Stage," stated Concacaf president and FIFA vice president Victor Montagliani. "Our fans want to see the best teams in our region compete against each other, and this format will create more opportunities for those matchups to happen earlier in the competition. At the same time, every match will matter, with teams facing a balanced mix of opponents and competing for a place in the knockout rounds. We believe this will make for a more competitive and exciting Gold Cup from the very first match through to the final.".

How matchups are determined is where things get a little confusing, as they will organize the eight teams into ranking bands of two teams each, with a predetermined fixture matrix ensuring that each team plays a balanced schedule of opponents.

This is to prevent a situation where two strong Concacaf sides essentially ensure that others don't have a chance to advance, which could lead to more interesting fixtures in the knockout stages depending on how it goes.

🚨🏆 The rumors are confirmed! Gold Cup will have a whole upcoming format in 2027. @FabrizioRomano breaks it down! pic.twitter.com/ydD1ZwbBvK.

Industry observers note that for the knockouts, nothing changes from how things used to look, as those four teams advancing from each group will then be placed into a single bracket, with the highest-finishing teams in each group facing off against the lower-finishing teams in the opposite group. There will then be no reseeding as the quarterfinals will determine the semifinal pairings in the road to the championship.

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

It was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

Recent findings suggest that this latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.

Yamal was orchestrating everything from the pace of the match to the volume of the supporters, at one point imploring them to raise the noise in the first half with both arms aloft.

There was also another impressive performance from England international Anthony Gordon and Raphinha, who dedicated his two goals to the memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife forward, who died on Tuesday.

With that tragedy fresh in the minds and the Nou Camp under construction, it was a peculiar atmosphere at times.

The defeat marked the end of Villa’s 100 per cent record in the competition, with a tough test away at Galatasaray up next before they host PSG in December. They remain high up in the table and have often displayed a propensity to bounce back rapidly from defeats.

Sources indicate that emery mentioned: “We are in a process and this was a very good test against a team like Barcelona. Nine years have passed since Emery’s last visit in this competition and time has not proved a great healer.

Industry observers note that that mistake could have threatened to damage confidence but Villa did respond. Matty Cash’s half-volley from inside the penalty area was only a few inches wide, while Johan Manzambi side-footed wide of the goal after a quick break down the right from Nicolas Jackson.

According to recent reports, with Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart and Jules Koundé all absent here, Barcelona’s defence did appear vulnerable. Emery was furious, appearing to raise his fist in the air at another poor goal conceded.

Unai Emery’s side will be relieved that they took a maximum nine points from their opening three games as their fixtures in this competition are getting a lot harder. This away game in Barcelona is followed up by a tricky trip to Turkey. Then it is tough back-to-back home games against PSG and Borussia Dortmund.

Unai Emery has managed more than 1,100 matches but will never forget the drama of “La Remontada” as he returns to the scene on Tuesday night.

Emery is back at the Nou Camp in the Champions League for the first time since one of the most epic games in the history of the competition. While in charge of Paris St-Germain nine years ago, Emery took his team to Barcelona with a 4-0 lead from the round-of-16 first leg. Yet he was left stunned as Barcelona recovered to win the rematch 6-1, with three goals in the final seven minutes and the winner proving hugely controversial.

Sergi Roberto’s goal five minutes into added time caused a massive backlash as PSG claimed it was offside, with Emery claiming on Monday that the match showed that VAR was “necessary”.

Aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

Sources indicate that aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

According to recent reports, “In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery said. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

Recent findings suggest that “[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

It has been revealed that barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

Sources indicate that “We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick remarked. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which demonstrated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

Team news from Nou Camp to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ravenna have announced their sold-out Serie C match featuring Ronaldinho’s return to the field earned them €199,000 in ticket sales alone at the Stadio Benelli.

The match against Forlì in the third division of Italian football turned into a global event that was transmitted live in many different countries, an entirely unusual occurrence for a club in the lower leagues.

The Stadio Benelli was even expanded for the event, with a latest temporary stand set up and named Tribuna R10 in honour of the Brazilian legend.

The Ravenna press office informed Football Italia that they raked in €199,000 in ticket sales on Sunday, thanks to a 6,743 sold-out crowd at the Stadio Benelli.

Ticket prices were inevitably raised for the big occasion, rising to a maximum of €150 for the hospitality section, but starting at €15 for season ticket holders, and under-14s able to attend for just €10.

Ronaldinho started the match and played the entire first half, using the break to salute the crowd and perhaps bow out for good at the age of 46.

#1507. Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino's Man United SQUAD AUDIT: Axe EIGHT stars, newly introduced role for the attacker he's 'always liked' and who could be his new Dele Alli... now give YOUR player-by-player verdict
